subject: social
name: Social Studies
title: Grade 11 Social Studies: United States History
overview: Grade 11 Social Studies prepares young citizens for active democratic participation and global engagement through rigorous historical, political, geographic, and economic inquiry.
competencies: Evaluate complex primary sources, detecting bias, corroborating claims, and synthesizing context.
Analyze constitutional principles, governmental structures, and civil liberties in a democratic republic.
Apply macroeconomic principles, market mechanics, and fiscal/monetary policies to public issues.
Deliberate contemporary global policy dilemmas using evidence-based civic discourse.

modules.title: Industrialization, the Gilded Age & the Progressive Era (1877–1920)
modules.description: Analyzing the rise of corporate trusts, robber barons, labor union strikes, immigration, and progressive social/political reforms.

topics.title: Industrial Capitalism, Monopolies and Urbanization
topics.description: Investigating Carnegie, Rockefeller, immigration at Ellis Island, sweatshops, and early labor unions.

topics.title: The Progressive Era Reforms and Constitutional Amendments
topics.description: Examining muckrakers (Tarbell, Sinclair), women's suffrage (19th Amendment), trust-busting, and conservation.

modules.title: The Great Depression, the New Deal & World War II (1929–1945)
modules.description: Analyzing the 1929 stock market crash, FDR's New Deal social safety net, and American industrial mobilization in WWII.

topics.title: The 1929 Crash, Dust Bowl and the New Deal
topics.description: Analyzing banking collapse, the TVA, Social Security, the Wagner Act, and debates over executive power.

topics.title: World War II: The Homefront and the Global Theater
topics.description: Japanese American internment, women in defense factories, the Manhattan Project, and the post-war superpower shift.

modules.title: The Cold War, the Civil Rights Movement & Contemporary America (1945–Present)
modules.description: Examining containment, Vietnam, the Civil Rights movement, Watergate, Reaganomics, and contemporary challenges.

topics.title: The Cold War at Home and Abroad: Korea, Cuba and Vietnam
topics.description: Analyzing the Truman Doctrine, McCarthyism, the Cuban Missile Crisis, and the anti-war movement.

topics.title: The African American Civil Rights Movement and Beyond
topics.description: Examining Brown v. Board of Education, the Montgomery Bus Boycott, MLK Jr., Malcolm X, and the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
